citation: Mishra SS, Stoklosinski H, Hedderley D, et al. Effect of Lamb and Soy Protein on Postprandial Glycaemic, Insulin and Appetite Responses to Potato, Pasta and Rice in Macronutrient-Equalised Meals—A Randomised Pilot Human Intervention Study. Nutrients. 2026;18(14):2351.
protocol: Nine meals, crossover: potato, pasta or rice (40 g available carbohydrate) alone, with lamb (30 g protein), or with soy protein; pasta sauce and lamb fat (12.6 g added where no lamb) equalised; Table 1 gives composition (protein meals ~34-37 g protein). Capillary samples at 0, 15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120, 150 min (check which times were used for insulin).
population: 15 healthy participants, no sign of glucose intolerance (Table 2 gives sex, age and BMI); New Zealand.

reports.where: Table 3: insulin iAUC mean and s.e. for each of 9 meals; Table 4: amplitude/peak

note: Shows how much protein (animal versus plant) raises insulin when added to the same carbohydrate dose, across three starches. Insulin is from capillary plasma by ELISA, in µU/mL·min. Only in figures: insulin time course (Figure 3). Meal kinds: mixed meal.
